script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

Title: FRESH START

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

A crisp autumn sun filters in through the kitchen window, casting warm light on the worn linoleum floor. The scent of bacon wafts through the air. JOANN, a woman in her late 40s, stands at the stove, a frypan in her hand.

JOANN
(talking to herself)
I can't believe it's already Thursday. This week's been a blur.

The doorbell rings, startling Joann. She turns off the stove and heads to the foyer.

INT. FOYER

Joann opens the door to reveal JIM, a man in his late 50s, carrying a small bouquet of flowers. He smiles, revealing a warm and genuine expression.

JIM
(cheerfully)
Good morning, Joann. I brought you breakfast.

Joann's face brightens.

JOANN
(delighted)
Jim! What a wonderful surprise! Come in.

INT. KITCHEN

Joann takes the flowers and sets them on the counter. Jim follows her into the kitchen, taking in the sight of the sunlit room and the aroma of bacon.

JIM
You always make my mornings brighter.

They share a laugh.

JOANN
Well, I could use some brightening myself. This week's been a doozy.

Jim takes a seat at the table as Joann pours them both cups of coffee.

INT. LIVING ROOM - AFTERNOON

Joann and Jim sit on the couch, surrounded by an array of resumes and job listings on the coffee table.

JOANN
(frustrated)
I can't believe I've been out of work for two months now. It feels like every opportunity I apply for slips through my fingers.

JIM
(supportively)
You're not alone, Joann. The job market's tough right now. But I believe in you. And I know you'll find something soon.

They share a reassuring look.

INT. JOANN'S STUDIO APARTMENT - NIGHT

Joann sits at her desk, surrounded by her art supplies. She looks at a photograph of herself as a young woman, holding a paintbrush and a smile. She sighs and sets the photograph aside, picking up a pencil instead. She begins to sketch, her focus intense.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Joann and Jim sit in a quiet corner of the coffee shop, their laptops open in front of them. They work in silence, the only sounds being the clinking of cups and the soft hum of conversation.

JOANN
(excitedly)
Jim, I think I might have something! This company posted a job listing for a graphic designer today, and I think I have just the right skills for it.

JIM
(encouragingly)
That's fantastic, Joann! I'll help you prepare your portfolio and resume for the interview. We'll make sure you stand out.

INT. JOANN'S APARTMENT - EVENING

Joann sits in front of her full-length mirror, dressed in her best interview attire. She takes a deep breath and smiles, the reflection of her face lighting up with confidence.

JOANN
(to herself)
I've got this.

INT. GRAPHIC DESIGN AGENCY - DAY

Joann waits nervously in the reception area, her heart pounding in her chest. She sees JIM across the room, sitting in a plush chair, reading a magazine. He nods at her in encouragement as she's called in for her interview.

INT. INTERVIEW ROOM - DAY

Joann sits across from the INTERVIEWER, a stern but fair-looking woman. She answers the interviewer's questions with confidence and eloquence, discussing her experiences and passion for graphic design.

INT. GRAPHIC DESIGN AGENCY - LATER THAT DAY

Joann sits in the reception area, her heart racing as she waits for the interviewer to make her decision. Jim enters the room, a smile on his face.

JIM
(excitedly)
Joann! I have fantastic news! They loved your portfolio and your interview went incredibly well. You've got the job!

Joann gasps in shock and joy, tears streaming down her face.

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

Joann and Jim sit at the kitchen table, drinking coffee and enjoying the morning sun.

JOANN
(gratefully)
I can't thank you enough, Jim. You were there for me every step of the way.

JIM
(smiling)
That's what friends are for, Joann. I'm just happy to see you getting a fresh start.

They share a warm, affectionate smile.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
